heads.la: INCIPIT SECUNDUS TOMUS Super hoc quod dicitur: Meliora sunt ubera tua vino, fragrantia unguentis optimis.
heads.en: HERE BEGINS THE SECOND TOME Upon that which is said: Thy breasts are better than wine, fragrant with the best ointments.

heads.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS, DE THRONO EBURNEO ET AUREO, QUALITER SUB ALLEGORICA INTERPRETATIONE REFERRI DEBEAT AD PERSONAM BEATAE, ET GLORIOSAE, ET PERPETUAE SEMPER VIRGINIS MARIAE.
heads.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING, CONCERNING THE THRONE OF IVORY AND GOLD, IN WHAT MANNER, UNDER AN ALLEGORICAL INTERPRETATION, IT OUGHT TO BE REFERRED TO THE PERSON OF THE BLESSED AND GLORIOUS AND PERPETUAL EVER-VIRGIN MARY.

heads.la: INCIPIT TERTIUS TOMUS Super hoc quod dicitur: Oleum effusum nomen tuum, ideo adolescentulae dilexerunt te nimis.
heads.en: HERE BEGINS THE THIRD TOME Upon that which is said: Thy name is oil poured out; therefore the maidens have loved thee exceedingly.

heads.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING ACCORDING TO THE MORAL SENSE.

heads.la: INCIPIT QUARTUS TOMUS Super hoc quod dicitur: Trahe me post te, curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum.
heads.en: HERE BEGINS THE FOURTH TOME Upon that which is said: Draw me after thee, we will run in the odour of thy ointments.

heads.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS SECUNDUM ALLEGORICUM ET MYSTICUM SENSUM.
heads.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING ACCORDING TO THE ALLEGORICAL AND MYSTICAL SENSE.

heads.la: INCIPIT QUINTUS TOMUS Super hoc quod dicitur: Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua, exsultabimus et laetabimur in te memores uberum tuorum: super vinum recti diligunt te.
heads.en: HERE BEGINS THE FIFTH TOME Upon that which is said: The king hath brought me into his storerooms, we will be glad and rejoice in thee, mindful of thy breasts: above wine the upright love thee [n: (Cant. I)].

heads.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS SECUNDUM MYSTICUM ET ALLEGORICUM SENSUM IN ILLA SENTENTIA: « INTRODUXIT ME REX IN CELLARIA SUA. »
heads.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING ACCORDING TO THE MYSTICAL AND ALLEGORICAL SENSE UPON THAT SENTENCE: « THE KING HATH BROUGHT ME INTO HIS STOREROOMS. »

heads.la: RECAPITULATIO SECUNDUM ANAGOGEN ET MORALITATEM IN ILLA SENTENTIA: « INTRODUXIT ME REX IN CELLARIA SUA. »
heads.en: RECAPITULATION ACCORDING TO THE ANAGOGE AND THE MORALITY UPON THAT SENTENCE: « THE KING HATH BROUGHT ME INTO HIS STOREROOMS. »

heads.la: INCIPIT SEXTUS TOMUS Ab eo quod dicitur: Nigra sum, sed formosa, filiae Jerusalem, usque ad vineam meam non custodivi.
heads.en: HERE BEGINS THE SIXTH TOME From that which is said: I am black, but comely, O daughters of Jerusalem, as far as my vineyard I have not kept [n: (Cant. I)].

heads.en: HOW THIS SENTENCE, « I AM BLACK, BUT COMELY, » IS ASCRIBED TO BLESSED MARY.

heads.la: INCIPIT SEPTIMUS TOMUS Super hoc quod dicitur: Indica mihi quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie, ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum.
heads.en: HERE BEGINS THE SEVENTH TOME Upon that which is said: Show me, thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest down at midday, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions [n: (Cant. I)].

heads.la: CONCLUSIO SENTENTIAE.
heads.en: CONCLUSION OF THE SENTENCE.

heads.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS, QUALITER AD PERSONAM PATRIS REFERRI DEBEAT ISTA SENTENTIA, SCILICET, « INDICA MIHI, » ETC.
heads.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING, IN WHAT MANNER THIS SENTENCE OUGHT TO BE REFERRED TO THE PERSON OF THE FATHER, NAMELY, « SHOW ME, » ETC.

headnotes.la: …llit. Qui ergo in capite, hoc est in mente, vitiorum telis vulnerati dolent, isti sine dubio necesse est ut auxilium et opem sanctae Dei Genitricis Mariae implorent, et ex intimo affectu cordis dicant
headnotes.en: … is, in the mind — being wounded by the darts of vices, it is needful without doubt that they implore the help and aid of holy Mary the Mother of God, and say from the innermost affection of the heart

headnotes.la: …tes vel naturas habere perhibetur, quae nomini Christi aptissime convenire videntur, quia juxta Isaiam prophetam [n: (cap. XI)], septem dona Spiritus sancti super ipsum requievisse dicuntur; scilicet,
headnotes.en: …rs or natures, which seem most aptly to agree with the name of Christ, since according to Isaiah the prophet [n: (cap. XI)] the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit are said to have rested upon him; namely,

headnotes.la: Sed jam ad septem naturas olei disserendas veniamus, et eas Domino Jesu coaptemus. Omnes liquores in quibus ponitur oleum supernatare fertur. Quod bene Domino Jesu congruit, quia sicut Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: …me to the discussing of the seven natures of oil, and fit them to the Lord Jesus. Oil is said to float above all liquids into which it is put. Which well agrees with the Lord Jesus, since as Paul says

headnotes.la: Et ipse Deus
headnotes.en: And God himself

headnotes.la: Oleum nullum externum liquorem recipit, quia Christum nulla peccati macula vel contagio infecit, sicut Petrus dicit
headnotes.en: Oil receives no external liquid, since no stain or contagion of sin infected Christ, as Peter says

headnotes.la: homines reficit, et Christus nos sanguine et carne sua potat et satiat. Vulnera sanat, quia Christus sicut Isaias ait
headnotes.en: it refreshes men, and Christ gives us his blood and his flesh to drink and satisfies us. It heals wounds, since Christ, as Isaiah says

headnotes.la: …ntiatus est. Compara ergo, si tibi placet, septem dona Spiritus sancti septem naturis olei, et considerabis mirabilia in lege Dei. Non *306* est major sapientia, quam ut cognoscat homo suum Creatorem,
headnotes.en: …, the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit with the seven natures of oil, and thou shalt consider wondrous things in the law of God. There is no *306* greater wisdom than that a man should know his Creator,

headnotes.la: …ione bimembri. Nec mirum sane si Sponsa sui Sponsi laudat clementiam, cum etiam ipse Sponsus non taceat affectum et pietatem quam habuerit erga Sponsam suam. Sic enim ipse dicit per Jeremiam prophetam
headnotes.en: …cy of her Bridegroom, since the Bridegroom himself also does not keep silent about the affection and tenderness which he has had toward his Bride. For thus he himself says through Jeremiah the prophet

headnotes.la: … vel in prophetis de oleo aliquid dictum potest reperiri, quod nomini sponsi congruat et in mysteriis Sponsae videlicet sanctae Ecclesiae decenter valeat aptari. In Exodo nempe dicit Dominus ad Moysen
headnotes.en: …thing said about oil can be found which agrees with the name of the Bridegroom and can becomingly be fitted to the mysteries of the Bride, that is, of holy Church. For in Exodus the Lord says to Moses

headnotes.la: Isaias quoque propheta olei mentionem faciens dicit
headnotes.en: Isaiah the prophet also, making mention of oil, says

headnotes.la: In Zacharia vero propheta de oleo sic scribitur
headnotes.en: But in Zechariah the prophet it is thus written of oil

headnotes.la: …eo aliquid sub allegorico sensu loquamur, quod et Christo et sanctae Ecclesiae congruat, et singulis quibusque fidelibus moraliter conveniat. Videamus ergo quid sit quod Isaias egregius propheta dicit
headnotes.en: …egorical sense, which may agree both with Christ and with holy Church, and may morally suit each and every one of the faithful. Let us see, therefore, what it is that Isaiah the excellent prophet says

headnotes.la: … ut valeam considerare mirabilia sacramenta, quae sunt ab aeterno abscondita in sancta ac beatissima lege tua. *Eleos* siquidem Graece, *misericordia* Latine dicitur. Dominus quippe in Evangelio dicit
headnotes.en: …le to consider the wondrous mysteries which are hidden from eternity in thy holy and most blessed law. *Eleos* indeed in Greek is called in Latin *misericordia*, mercy. For the Lord says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: David quoque propheta refectus Spiritus sancti superabundanti gratia, de Deo sic loquitur
headnotes.en: David the prophet also, refreshed by the superabundant grace of the Holy Spirit, speaks thus of God

headnotes.la: … divinitatis excessit, sicut solet cornu illam carnem excedere de qua oriendo videtur procedere. De hoc autem cornu, id est de incarnatione Domini Jesu Zacharias impletus Spiritus sancti gratia dixit,
headnotes.en: …s that flesh out of which, in rising, it is seen to proceed. But concerning this horn, that is, concerning the incarnation of the Lord Jesus, Zacharias, filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit, said,

headnotes.la: Et quasi si aliquis quaereret ab eo quam misericordiam Deus Israel fecisset populo suo, protinus adjunxit, dicens
headnotes.en: And as though someone were asking of him what mercy the God of Israel had done to his people, he straightway added, saying

headnotes.la: …ilio olei, id est per humanitatem quam assumpsit, sanctam Ecclesiam sibi acquisivit Filius omnipotentis Dei. Quod autem ipse Filius, dilectus appelletur, Sponsa ejus in Canticis canticorum protestatur
headnotes.en: … of oil; that is, through the humanity which he took, the Son of almighty God acquired holy Church for himself. But that the Son himself is called beloved, his Bride bears witness in the Song of Songs

headnotes.la: Rubicundus propter sanguinis in cruce effusionem, candidus ob virginitatis et castitatis praerogativam. Item in eodem libello charissima ejus Sponsa sicut de eodem Sponso suo loquitur
headnotes.en: …because of the shedding of blood on the cross; white, because of the prerogative of virginity and chastity. Again in the same little book his most dear Bride speaks thus of the same Bridegroom of hers

headnotes.la: …uae in Isaia appellatur vinea, ipsa in Canticis canticorum dicitur Sponsa. Ista vinea quidem effecta est in deliciis charissima dilecto Filio olei, ex quo ex ea carnem accepit, quia sicut dicit Paulus
headnotes.en: …d a vineyard, is herself called Bride in the Song of Songs. This vineyard indeed was made most dear in delights to the beloved Son of oil, from the time when he took flesh from her, since as Paul says

headnotes.la: Et alio in loco idem Paulus manifestius insinuat quam dilectionem Sponsus erga Sponsam suam habeat
headnotes.en: And in another place the same Paul more plainly intimates what love the Bridegroom has toward his Bride

headnotes.la: Unde idem Sponsus in Canticis canticorum de Sponsa sua dicit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Ephes. V, 25 *sicut et Christus dilexit ecclesiam, et se ipsum tradidit pro ea*] Whence the same Bridegroom in the Song of Songs says of his Bride

headnotes.la: …m in Isaia, verum in libro Evangeliorum et in Canticis canticorum: in Evangelio autem ubi paterfamilias operarios in vineam suam conduxit [n: (Matth. XX)]; in Canticis vero canticorum ubi scriptum est
headnotes.en: …in Isaiah, but in the book of the Gospels and in the Song of Songs: in the Gospel, where the householder hired workmen into his vineyard [n: (Matth. XX)]; but in the Song of Songs, where it is written

headnotes.la: et,
headnotes.en: and,

headnotes.la: … quando eam eloquiis prophetarum munivit, et, ne conculcari et dilacerari queat ab haereticis, quasi forti praesidio, apostolicis erudivit documentis. Unde bene quidem sequitur in eodem propheta, quia
headnotes.en: …the prophets, and, lest it could be trodden down and torn asunder by heretics, instructed it with apostolic teachings as with a strong garrison. Whence it well indeed follows in the same prophet, that

headnotes.la: … itaque qui in Evangelio zizania vocantur [n: (Matth. XIII)], ipsi in Isaia propheta lapides appellantur, et in Canticis canticorum eleganti sermone sub nomine vulpium describuntur, sicut scriptum est
headnotes.en: … the Gospel are called cockle [n: (Matth. XIII)], are themselves called stones in Isaiah the prophet, and in the Song of Songs are described in elegant speech under the name of foxes, as it is written

headnotes.la: Quod autem Propheta dicit: [Et plantavit illam electam], hoc est nimirum, quod Dominus in Evangelio ait
headnotes.en: But what the Prophet says: [And he planted it a choice vine], this doubtless is what the Lord says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Et Paulus apostolus in Epistolis suis
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Joan. XV, 16 *ego elegi vos et posui vos, ut eatis*; *de mundo* stands at verse 19] And Paul the apostle in his Epistles

headnotes.la: et Dei
headnotes.en: and, of God

headnotes.la: De apostolis vero dicitur
headnotes.en: But of the apostles it is said

headnotes.la: Turris quoque quam propheta Isaias in medio vineae aedificatam testatur fuisse, ipsa siquidem est nomen Domini, de quo per Salomonem dicitur
headnotes.en: The tower too, which the prophet Isaiah testifies to have been built in the midst of the vineyard, is itself the name of the Lord, of which it is said through Solomon

headnotes.la: Homines namque ideo ad turrim confugiunt ut ab infestatione hostium liberari queant. Bene itaque nomen Domini turri comparatur in qua homines salvantur, quia sicut ait Petrus apostolus
headnotes.en: …n flee to a tower for this reason, that they may be freed from the harassing of enemies. And so the name of the Lord is well compared to a tower in which men are saved, since as Peter the apostle says

headnotes.la: …inas et labruscas, id est inutiles fructus et noxios Domino generant et apportant. Verumtamen quid de talibus in die judicii fieri debeat propheta in subsequentibus suae narrationis manifestat, dicens
headnotes.en: …pes instead of grapes, that is, useless and harmful fruits. But nevertheless what ought to be done with such men on the day of judgment the prophet makes plain in what follows in his narrative, saying

headnotes.la: …re debemus, quos sine dubio illius coelestis Jerusalem quae sursum est mater nostra, cives et habitatores esse scimus. Quibus itaque remota omni ambiguitate Dominus in Evangelio suo repromittit dicens
headnotes.en: … saints, whom without doubt we know to be citizens and inhabitants of that heavenly Jerusalem which is above, our mother. And so to them, all ambiguity removed, the Lord promises in his Gospel, saying

headnotes.la: Et Paulus apostolus
headnotes.en: And Paul the apostle

headnotes.la: Et alio in loco de omnibus sanctis scriptum est
headnotes.en: And in another place it is written of all the saints

headnotes.la: De istis videlicet apostolis et caeteris sanctis coram majestate Dei in aeterna jam praedestinatione sublimatis, Zacharias propheta gloriam eorum contemplatus prophetavit, dicens
headnotes.en: Of these apostles, namely, and of the other saints, already exalted before the majesty of God in eternal predestination, Zechariah the prophet, contemplating their glory, prophesied, saying

headnotes.la: Quae sit autem vinea idem propheta manifestius declarat cum dicit
headnotes.en: But what the vineyard is the same prophet declares more plainly when he says

headnotes.la: De hac quoque vinea loquitur David propheta
headnotes.en: Of this vineyard David the prophet also speaks

headnotes.la: et caetera quae sequuntur in ipso psalmo de eadem vinea quae facile possunt intelligi sine interpretatione aliqua. Haec est, inquam, illa vinea scilicet plebs Judaica, de qua Salvator in Evangelio ait
headnotes.en: … in that psalm concerning the same vineyard, which can easily be understood without any interpretation. This, I say, is that vineyard, namely the Jewish people, of which the Saviour says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …colis interficitur Dominus Jesus Christus est, qui a summis sacerdotibus et scribis et pharisaeis crucifigitur. Sed jam ad superiorem sententiam redeamus, de qua sub typo Synagogae loqui disposueramus
headnotes.en: …Jesus Christ, who is crucified by the high priests and the scribes and the Pharisees. But let us now return to the foregoing saying, of which we had purposed to speak under the figure of the Synagogue

headnotes.la: De isto namque dilecto ipso charissimo loquitur Sponsa in eodem de quo loquimur libro
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Luc. IX, 35 *hic est Filius meus electus, ipsum audite*, "my chosen son"] For of this beloved, this most dear one, the Bride speaks in the very book of which we are speaking

headnotes.la: …t diabolus, illam devastaret. Idcirco enim vinea sepitur ut Domino ipsius vineae fructus ejus illaesus conservetur, et hostibus, et animalibus claustra ipsius non facile reserentur. Quod autem dicitur
headnotes.en: …eyard is hedged in for this reason, that its fruit may be kept unharmed for the lord of that vineyard, and that its barriers may not be easily unbarred to enemies and to beasts. But as to what is said

headnotes.la: …onstat quia post electionem apostolorum expulsa sit ipsa Synagoga a Deo et abjecta. De qua utique abjectione bene in Isaia scriptum reperitur, ubi Dominus de Sobna Scriba et praeposito templi loquitur
headnotes.en: …ction of the apostles that Synagogue was driven out by God and cast off. And of this casting-off it is well found written in Isaiah, where the Lord speaks of Sobna the scribe and provost of the temple

headnotes.la: Simili quoque modo de abjectione Synagogae sub persona Jeconiae regis scriptum est
headnotes.en: …clause here; the words about the station stand at verse 19 as *et expellam te de statione tua*] In like manner also it is written of the casting-off of the Synagogue under the person of king Jechonias

headnotes.la: …naceum novimus esse animal castratum et infructuosum, cui bene antiqua lex comparatur, quae sicut dicit beatus Paulus, nihil ad perfectum adduxit, unde merito sequitur in Isaia propheta de eodem Sobna
headnotes.en: …ated and unfruitful, to which the ancient law is well compared, which, as blessed Paul says, brought nothing to perfection; whence it deservedly follows in Isaiah the prophet concerning the same Sobna

headnotes.la: …atio degeneravit ab illa gloriosa et paterna vita, de cujus radice videbatur propaginem ducere. Quam utique degenerationem Dominus in Evangelio, benignissima improperatione Judaeis exprobrabat, dicens
headnotes.en: …ch degenerated from that glorious and fatherly life, from whose root it seemed to draw its shoot. Which degeneration the Lord in the Gospel reproached to the Jews with a most kindly upbraiding, saying

headnotes.la: …ia ad Judaeos maxime pertineat. Nonne ipsi Judaei pro uvis labruscas attulerunt, quando Creatorem suum ante faciem Pilati negaverunt? [n: (Joan. XIX.)] Quod utique beatus Petrus eis improperat, dicens
headnotes.en: …e Jews. Did not the Jews themselves bring wild grapes instead of grapes, when they denied their Creator before the face of Pilate? [n: (Joan. XIX.)] Which indeed blessed Peter upbraids to them, saying

headnotes.la: Nonne Judaei sceleratissimi labruscas Domino fecerunt pro uvis, quando dixerunt Pilato
headnotes.en: …var: Vulg. Act. III, 15 *auctorem vero vitae interfecistis*, "but you killed the author of life"] Did not the most wicked Jews make wild grapes for the Lord instead of grapes, when they said to Pilate

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: Propterea illud quod Isaias dicit in subseqnentibus
headnotes.en: Therefore that which Isaiah says in what [sic: *subseqnentibus*]

headnotes.la: …tinere ad generalem resurrectionem nullus ignorat, in qua sancti apostoli istam vineam judicabunt et condemnabunt. Hoc denique Dominus in Evangelio ipsis Judaeis sibi detrahentibus, testatur cum dicit
headnotes.en: … the general resurrection, in which the holy apostles shall judge and condemn that vineyard. This, in fine, the Lord in the Gospel testifies to the Jews themselves as they disparaged him, when he says

headnotes.la: Ideo ipsi vestri judices erunt. Quod etiam iste Isaias propheta declarat, cum de adventu Domini et sanctorum apostolorum ad diem judicii prophetavit, dicens
headnotes.en: …nes*] Therefore they themselves shall be your judges. Which this same prophet Isaiah also declares, when he prophesied of the coming of the Lord and of the holy apostles to the day of judgment, saying

headnotes.la: Salomon quoque Christum, et sanctam Ecclesiam, et sanctos apostolos, et diem judicii brevi sermone curavit comprehendere cum dicit
headnotes.en: …d judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus*] Solomon too took care to comprise in a brief speech Christ, and holy Church, and the holy apostles, and the day of judgment, when he says

headnotes.la: …istere Dominatori universae terrae. Quod ideo per binarium numerum descripsit, quia eos prophetico spiritu divinitatem et humanitatem Christi praedicare praevidit. Porro illud quod idem propheta dicit
headnotes.en: … Which he described by the number two for this reason, that he foresaw in the prophetic spirit that they would preach the divinity and the humanity of Christ. Further, that which the same prophet says

headnotes.la: non solum de apostolis, verum etiam de omnibus sanctis dictum esse intelligamus. Unde Domiuus ipse in Evangelio suo ait
headnotes.en: let us understand to have been said not only of the apostles, but also of all the saints. Whence the [sic: *Domiuus*] himself in his Gospel says

headnotes.la: Quod etiam beatus Augustinus doctor egregius, et catholicae fidei defensor fidelissimus testatur cum dicit
headnotes.en: …illic et minister meus erit*, "where I am, there also shall my minister be"] Which blessed Augustine also, the excellent doctor and most faithful defender of the catholic faith, testifies when he says

headnotes.la: …eritus et male morigeratus disputet de bonis moribus hominum, tamen nequaquam sopitis sensibus negligere debemus, quod semper et sine intervallo benedicere et laudare Deum jubemur, sicut Psalmista ait
headnotes.en: …ed man should dispute about the good morals of men, yet we ought in no wise, with drowsy senses, to neglect that we are bidden always and without interval to bless and praise God, as the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: …efficax potestas, sicque tandem poterimus *311* Deo ampliante adipisci, ut simus boni et perfecti, laudibusque Dei idonei. Sed jam nunc discutiamus sententiam istam sub morali interpretatione scilicet
headnotes.en: … at length we shall be able, God enlarging us, to attain that we may be good and perfect and *311* fit for the praises of God. But now let us examine this saying under the moral interpretation, namely

headnotes.la: Beatus ille homo licet mortalis sit, cujus nomen ob meritum bonae vitae tantam praerogativam jam obtinuit, ut illi veraciter dici possit
headnotes.en: Blessed is that man, though he be mortal, whose name for the desert of a good life has already obtained so great a prerogative that it can truly be said to him

headnotes.la: … sibi non vult fieri, alteri non facit, et qui in omnibus operibus suis quaerit ut Deus laudetur, et qui talem se exhibet ut ab omnibus hominibus pro sanctitate sua veneretur, isti nimirum dici potest
headnotes.en: … he does not wish to be done to himself, and who in all his works seeks that God be praised, and who so shows himself that he is venerated by all men for his holiness — to him doubtless it can be said

headnotes.la: …ad Dominum convertantur, et insuper qui columbina pace et fraterna dilectione animis fratrum suorum amabilem se reddit, adeo, ut ab omnibus pura mentis intentione diligatur, huic sine dubio dici debet
headnotes.en: …er who by dove-like peace and brotherly love makes himself lovable to the minds of his brethren, so far that he is loved by all with a pure intention of mind — to him without doubt it ought to be said

headnotes.la: id est fratrum animae,
headnotes.en: that is, the souls of the brethren,

headnotes.la: …ostri sunt, de quibus dicit beatus Paulus: Isti sunt viri misericordiae, quorum justitiae oblivionem ante Deum non acceperunt. Istae siquidem sunt arbores olivarum de quibus in Evangelio Dominus dicit
headnotes.en: …ly Fathers, of whom blessed Paul says: "These are men of mercy, whose righteousnesses have not received forgetfulness before God." These indeed are the olive trees of which the Lord says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Oleum harum arborum est omne opus bonum, pium, modestum, castum, religiosum, et sanctum. Quod autem per oleum, opus bonum intelligi debeat, Evangelium secundum Matthaeum manifestissime declarat
headnotes.en: …18] The oil of these trees is every work good, loving, modest, chaste, religious and holy. But that by the oil a good work ought to be understood, the Gospel according to Matthew most plainly declares

headnotes.la: Cui sententiae Salomon concordare satis videtur, qui inter caetera verba sua sic loquitur
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Matth. XXV, 1 *simile erit regnum caelorum*, future "shall be like"] With which saying Solomon seems well enough to agree, who among his other words speaks thus

headnotes.la: …stra anima induitur, dum in hoc corpusculo secundum Dei dispositionem demoratur. Quae utique membra semper debent candida esse, quia non debent alicui peccato subjacere. Sic enim dicit Isaias propheta
headnotes.en: …s clothed, while it tarries in this little body according to the disposition of God. Which members ought always to be white, since they ought not to lie under any sin. For thus says Isaiah the prophet

headnotes.la: Denique et Apostolus dicit
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Isa. IX, 5 *erit in combustionem et cibus ignis*, "shall be for burning, and fuel for the fire"] And moreover the Apostle says

headnotes.la: Et iterum
headnotes.en: And again

headnotes.la: …icit de capite nostro, quando mens nostra semper pio opere abundat, et bono desiderio. Et amplius, si fieri posset, vult assidue facere, quam unquam valeat ad perfectum perducere, unde Psalmista dicit
headnotes.en: … from our head when our mind always abounds in loving work and in good desire. And it wishes to do continually more, if it could be done, than it can ever bring to perfection; whence the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: …Exod. XXVII)], hoc significat nimirum, quia intentio *312* cordis nostri nunquam debet removeri a consideratione et contemplatione majestatis Dei, sicut illius cor a Deo nunquam recedebat, qui dicebat
headnotes.en: …ubtless signifies that the intention *312* of our heart ought never to be withdrawn from the consideration and contemplation of the majesty of God, as the heart of him never withdrew from God who said

headnotes.la: …ique oculum sancti Patres nostri interpretati sunt animi intentionem, vel sincerum mentis affectum. Tabernaculum vero testimonii, corpus nostrum non immerito potest intelligi, unde beatus Petrus dicit
headnotes.en: …thers have interpreted as the intention of the mind, or the sincere affection of the mind. And by the tabernacle of the testimony our body can not undeservedly be understood, whence blessed Peter says

headnotes.la: … assidue in tabernaculo nostro, cum fervor charitatis nunquam tepescit in corde nostro. Sic quippe ista lucerna charitatis in corde Pauli renitebat fulgore mirae claritatis, ita ut idem Paulus diceret
headnotes.en: …le when the fervour of charity never grows lukewarm in our heart. For thus that lamp of charity shone again in the heart of Paul with the brightness of a wondrous clearness, so that the same Paul said

headnotes.la: …sionem Spiritus sancti assidue cogitat, quae sunt Dei. Sicut ergo capitulum in libro Exodi secundum moralitatem discussimus: sic decens est, ut illam sententiam de Isaia assumptam moraliter disseramus
headnotes.en: …the things which are of God. As therefore we have examined the chapter in the book of Exodus according to the moral sense, so it is fitting that we discourse morally upon that saying taken from Isaiah

headnotes.la: …tam animam, cujus corpus etsi coram hominibus apparet publico, tamen in praesentia Dei manet in occulto, quia magis placere Deo studet interius, quam hominibus vel saeculo exterius, unde ait Psalmista
headnotes.en: …, whose body, though it appear publicly before men, yet in the presence of God remains in secret, since he strives to please God more inwardly than men or the world outwardly; whence the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: Hinc etiam Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: Hence Paul also says

headnotes.la: … fuerit quanto prius exstitit charior, pretiosior, acceptior atque amabilior, tanto postea exstat vilior, degenerior atque inutilior. Quod utique Dominus per prophetam Ezechielem manifestat, cum dicit
headnotes.en: …more precious, more acceptable and more lovable, by so much afterward it stands more vile, more degenerate and more useless. Which indeed the Lord makes plain through the prophet Ezekiel, when he says

headnotes.la: …ur, nonne isti merito *313* suae iniquitatis se tradunt ultricibus flammis velut vitis amputata et inutilis? Quibus procul dubio elegantissime illud congruit, quod Moyses propheta in suo cantico dicit
headnotes.en: …edly, for their *313* iniquity, hand themselves over to avenging flames like a lopped-off and useless vine? To whom beyond doubt that most elegantly agrees which Moses the prophet says in his canticle

headnotes.la: …onasterii septa, nomine tenus retinentur, quamvis, ut superius dixi, universum per orbem perdita mente, et animo volatili evagantur. Quibus nimirum bene convenit illud quod Dominus per prophetam dicit
headnotes.en: …f some sort, in name only, although, as I said above, with a lost mind and a flighty spirit they stray through the whole world. To whom indeed that well applies which the Lord says through the prophet

headnotes.la: …itia repugnantia, cogitationesque malae, et concupiscentiae carnales, quae nos a Deo alienant, si in nobis per nostram ignaviam principatum obtineant. De his siquidem alienis David conqueritur, dicens
headnotes.en: …hat fight against us, and evil thoughts, and carnal concupiscences, which estrange us from God, if by our own sloth they obtain the chief place in us. Of these strangers indeed David complains, saying

headnotes.la: Salomon quoque ait
headnotes.en: Solomon too says

headnotes.la: Et quasi nos quaereremus a Salomone qui essent isti alieni, illico subjunxit
headnotes.en: And as though we were asking of Solomon who these strangers were, he straightway added

headnotes.la: scilicet, diabolo, de quo Dominus testatur
headnotes.en: namely, the devil, of whom the Lord testifies

headnotes.la: …versas partes orbis terrarum girovagi peragrantur, vel, proh dolor! quod infamius est, ad saeculum revertuntur. Quibus nimirum decenter illud convenit, quod beatus Petrus apostolus in sua epistola ait
headnotes.en: …e diverse parts of the round world, or — alas the grief! — what is more infamous, they return to the world. To whom assuredly that fittingly belongs which the blessed apostle Peter says in his epistle

headnotes.la: Et
headnotes.en: And

headnotes.la: … projiciantur et ardeant. Longius ab ordine itaque nostrae narrationis digressi sumus, dum de natura vitis et vineae disputavimus, verumtamen jam idoneum est tempus ut revertamur ad id quod coeperamus
headnotes.en: …ore, from the order of our narration have we digressed, while we disputed of the nature of the vine and of the vineyard; nevertheless it is now a fitting time that we return to that which we had begun

headnotes.la: Dilectus itaque est, ad quem sponsa in Canticis canticorum legatos suos mittit, dicens
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Isa. 5:1 *Vinea facta est dilecto meo in cornu filio olei*, without *charissima*] The beloved, therefore, is he to whom the bride in the Song of Songs sends her legates, saying

headnotes.la: … interiit amor deceptoris hujus mundi. et ad nihilum redacta est fallax gloria fluentis saeculi. Huic siquidem dilecto sponso suo adhuc loquitur eadem sponsa sua charissima in delicis in eodem libello
headnotes.en: …ow utterly perished. And the deceitful glory of the flowing age has been brought to nothing. To this her beloved bridegroom that same most dear bride still speaks amid delights in the same little book

headnotes.la: …rium apparuit, ab Habacuch propheta *(Habac. III)* cornua in manibus habere perhibetur, in quibus nimirum maxima ejus fortitudo fuisse dignoscitur. Sic quippe in Cantico ejusdem prophetae scriptum est
headnotes.en: …eclared by the prophet Habacuc *(Habac. III)* to have horns in his hands, in which assuredly his greatest strength is discerned to have been. For thus it is written in the Canticle of the same prophet

headnotes.la: scilicet Christi, et in sequentibus
headnotes.en: namely Christ's, and in what follows

headnotes.la: …raeterea si nos vellemus modo ad medium ducere, quidquid de istis spiritualibus cornibus divina eloquia solent eloqui, facilius *314* nos dies desereret quam copia dicendi. Sed neque ex toto silebimus
headnotes.en: …er the divine eloquences are wont to utter concerning these spiritual horns, the day would more easily fail *314* us than the abundance of matter for speaking. But neither will we be silent altogether

headnotes.la: … quod vinea facta est charissima dilecto filio olei, id est anima nostra propter virtutes quas habet, diligitur et in magno honore habetur ab Unigenito Filio Dei, et hoc est quod per prophetam dicitur
headnotes.en: … the beloved son of oil, that is, that our soul, on account of the virtues which it has, is loved and held in great honour by the Only-begotten Son of God; and this is what is said through the prophet

headnotes.la: …pitionem intelligere nos convenit. O quam gloriosa et quam virtutibus praeclara est anima illa, de qua tanta est cura Deo, ut pia diligentia sepiatur ab ipso! Sic enim ipse Dominus dicit per prophetam
headnotes.en: …d of God. O how glorious and how illustrious in virtues is that soul, of which God has so great care, that it is fenced by him with loving diligence! For thus the Lord himself says through the prophet

headnotes.la: …quamvis adhuc morentur in terra pro infirmitate carnis, assidue tamen cum Christo sunt in coelo, et ei haerent spiritalibus desideriis? unde unus ex hujusmodi spiritalibus palis in terra degens aiebat
headnotes.en: …y still tarry on earth for the infirmity of the flesh, are yet assiduously with Christ in heaven, and cleave to him with spiritual desires? whence one of such spiritual stakes, dwelling on earth, said

headnotes.la: …? Istis ergo palis et hujusmodi virgis sepit Deus vineam suam, quia exemplis et doctrinis sanctorum suorum quotidie excolit, docet, instruit, et monet animas fidelium suorum. Hinc est quod David dixit
headnotes.en: … rods of this sort God fences his vineyard, because by the examples and teachings of his saints he daily tills, teaches, instructs and admonishes the souls of his faithful. Hence it is that David said

headnotes.la: Alius quoque propheta nihilominus ex persona Dei testatur, dicens
headnotes.en: …uitu timentium eum et eripiet eos*, "the angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him, and shall deliver them"] Another prophet likewise no less testifies in the person of God, saying

headnotes.la: …s ex ista vinea eligere et projicere, id est ab anima nostra omnia vitia quae ei displicent exstirpare; quatenus anima nostra veluti bonus palmes in ipso qui est vera vitis manens cum apostolis audiat
headnotes.en: …rth the stones from that vineyard, that is, to root out of our soul all the vices that displease him; that so our soul, as a good branch abiding in him who is the true vine, may hear with the apostles

headnotes.la: Quod autem in sequentibus suae narrationis dicit Isaias, quia
headnotes.en: But as to what Isaias says in the sequel of his narration, that

headnotes.la: ad nostrum corpus haec sciamus pertinere moraliter et ad nostram animam
headnotes.en: let us know that these things pertain morally to our body and to our soul

headnotes.la: Satis nimirum ista plantatio electa exstitit, quae ad similitudinem et imaginem Dei creata fuit. Praeterea in libro Sapientiae scriptum reperitur
headnotes.en: That planting was assuredly choice enough, which was created to the likeness and image of God. Moreover in the book of Wisdom it is found written

headnotes.la: … aedificii lapides. Coementum vero quod lapides ligat et complectitur, ipsa sit charitas sine qua nullum opus bonum esse dicitur, et in qua omne opus bonum solidatur et fundatur; sic enim dicit Paulus
headnotes.en: …building. And let the cement which binds and embraces the stones be charity itself, without which no work is said to be good, and in which every good work is made solid and founded; for thus says Paul

headnotes.la: … est omnibus opus quod in torculari agitur. In torculari quippe uvae exprimuntur et expressae liquefiunt, ut in vinum dulcissimum convertantur. Quamvis ergo Dominus de passione sua dicat per prophetam
headnotes.en: …ess. For in the winepress the grapes are pressed out, and being pressed out they melt, that they may be turned into most sweet wine. Although therefore the Lord says of his passion through the prophet

headnotes.la: …ffusio, non incongrue torcular animae appellari debet. Hoc torcular spirituale, exstructum in se habebat, illa charissima sponsa in deliciis quae in Canticis canticorum suspirans de Sponso suo dicebat
headnotes.en: …ught not unfittingly to be called the winepress of the soul. This spiritual winepress that most dear bride amid delights had built within her, who in the Song of Songs, sighing of her Bridegroom, said

headnotes.la: …ius non solum paulominus ab angelis minoratus de caelo descendit, sed etiam usque ad ignominiosae mortis supplicium pervenit. Quod equidem Jeremias propheta in suis lamentationibus protestatur, dicens
headnotes.en: …her not only came down from heaven a little lower than the angels, but even came as far as the punishment of an ignominious death. Which indeed the prophet Jeremias attests in his lamentations, saying

headnotes.la: … est quod sequitur in Isaia propheta. Et exspectavit, inquit Isaias, vineam suam Dominus ut faceret uvas, et ecce, proh dolor! fecit labruscas. Quae nimirum sententia potius est timenda quam exponenda
headnotes.en: …aias. And the Lord, says Isaias, looked for his vineyard to bring forth grapes, and behold, alas the grief! it brought forth wild grapes. Which sentence assuredly is rather to be feared than expounded

headnotes.la: …se sentientes errasse, toto cordis affectu ad religionem sanctam conversi sunt, et spreta saeculi vanitate totis viribus servitio Dei se mancipaverunt. De quibus Zacharias propheta mihi videtur dicere
headnotes.en: …ffection of the heart to holy religion, and, the vanity of the world despised, delivered themselves over with all their strength to the service of God. Of whom the prophet Zacharias seems to me to say

headnotes.la: …Sed hoc constat pro certo quoniam quidem si Deus oleum dicitur, hi qui sunt filii olei, aeque possunt dici et filii Dei. Cui siquidem sententiae consona voce concordat beatus Joannes apostolus, dicens
headnotes.en: …tands for certain, that if God is called oil, they who are the sons of oil can equally be called also the sons of God. To which sentence the blessed apostle John accords with a consonant voice, saying

headnotes.la: Consideremus ergo quis sit ille qui loquitur. Conversus nempe erat, apostolus et Evangelista erat, mundo abrenuntiaverat, ideoque; audacter aiebat
headnotes.en: …pparuit*, "it hath not yet appeared"] Let us consider then who he is that speaks. He was a convert indeed, he was an apostle and an Evangelist, he had renounced the world, and therefore he said boldly

headnotes.la: …amenti dignetur nobis inferre, ut secundum voluntatem ejus sensum spiritualem in litteris peplo obscuriori coopertis, valeamus reperire. Et enim velamen magnum super istam sententiam positum, scilicet
headnotes.en: … the letter of the Old Testament, so that according to his will we may be able to find the spiritual sense in letters covered with a darker robe. For indeed a great veil set over that sentence, namely

headnotes.la: …t a Sponso suo trahi se postulat, quandoquidem ista spiritalis attractio ad Patrem maxime ex auctoritate Filii ejus pertineat. Sic enim idem Filius Dei de eodem charissimo Patre suo dicit in Evangelio
headnotes.en: …by her Bridegroom, since indeed that spiritual attraction belongs chiefly to the Father by the authority of his Son. For thus the same Son of God says of the same most dear Father of his in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Denique idem piissimus Pater de eadem praeclara et praeelecta Filii sui Sponsa, id est sancta Ecclesia, per Jeremiam prophetam ait
headnotes.en: …xcept the Father, who hath sent me, draw him"] Finally that same most loving Father says of the same illustrious and fore-chosen Bride of his Son, that is, of holy Church, through Jeremias the prophet

headnotes.la: …t omnibus modis charitativa et voluntaria. Hinc est namque quod Psalmista spirituali desiderio inflammatus, ut laudes Dei digne pronuntiare valeat, attrahit gratiam Spiritus sancti, sicut scriptum est
headnotes.en: …e and voluntary. Hence it is indeed that the Psalmist, inflamed with spiritual desire, that he may be able worthily to utter the praises of God, draws in the grace of the Holy Spirit, as it is written

headnotes.la: subauditur sanctum, et in quid attraxisset eum manifeste subjunxit, dicens
headnotes.en: — the holy is understood; and for what he had drawn him in he manifestly subjoined, saying

headnotes.la: …m tuorum, quatenus charitate tua dilatati recipere valeamus infra armaliolum cordis nostri, charismata Spiritus sancti. Curramus ergo, fratres charissimi in odorem unguentorum Dei, ut dicatur de nobis
headnotes.en: …may be able to receive within the [sic: *armaliolum*] of our heart the charisms of the Holy Spirit. Let us run therefore, most dear brethren, in the odour of God's ointments, that it may be said of us

headnotes.la: *317* Ipso auxiliante qui ait
headnotes.en: *317* By the help of him who said

headnotes.la: …s, et freti sacrosancta aspiratione ipsius qui primum diem fecit, quid sacramenti ipsum opus in se contineat, salva sanctorum Patrum omnimoda expositione, mens nostra in lucem proferre non pertimescat
headnotes.en: …ost holy inspiration of him who made the first day, let not our mind be afraid to bring to light what of sacrament that work contains in itself, saving the exposition of the holy Fathers in every kind

headnotes.la: …i intimavit quod Deus in principio fecit coelum et terram, nisi ipse idem qui haec omnia ad laudem et honorem, et gloriam nominis sui condidit? Sed in quo principio? In eo nimirum qui ait in Evangelio
headnotes.en: …e beginning made heaven and earth, unless that same one who founded all these things to the praise and honour and glory of his name? But in what beginning? In that one assuredly who says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: In eo, inquam, de quo Joannes evangelista testatur
headnotes.en: In him, I say, of whom John the evangelist testifies

headnotes.la: In eo, inquam, de quo Psalmista ad Patrem dicit
headnotes.en: In him, I say, of whom the Psalmist says to the Father

headnotes.la: …, omnes leges illarum septem artium, quae secundum philosophiam liberales vocantur, reperiemus. Ut enim ad rhetoricam artem accedamus, juxta locutionis modos qui flores dicuntur, prima oratio scilicet
headnotes.en: …f those seven arts which according to philosophy are called liberal. For, that we may come to the art of rhetoric, according to the modes of speech which are called flowers, the first sentence, namely

headnotes.la: unimembris esse dignoscitur. Secundam vero orationem videlicet
headnotes.en: is discerned to be of one member. But the second sentence, to wit

headnotes.la: … sancto procedit, quae non solum in hoc libro, *318* verum etiam in omnibus divinis voluminibus repetitur, ista dixisse sufficiat. Beatus Augustinus super coelo et terra talem profert interpretationem
headnotes.en: …ich is repeated not only in this book, *318* but also in all the divine volumes, let it suffice to have said these things. The blessed Augustine puts forth such an interpretation upon heaven and earth

headnotes.la: …ossumus salvo sensu ecclesiasticae regulae, coelum et terram ad personam primi patris nostri Adae allegorice referre. Ipse enim antequam peccaret velut coelum exstitit, sed post peccatum a Deo audivit
headnotes.en: …ense of the ecclesiastical rule, refer heaven and earth allegorically to the person of our first father Adam. For he himself, before he sinned, stood as it were heaven, but after sin he heard from God

headnotes.la: …oriam sine gustu mortis pervenisset. Potest adhuc Adam alio modo coelum et terra nuncupari, quia ipse animam de coelesti natura habuit, et corpus ejus de terra originem duxit. Sic enim Scriptura dicit
headnotes.en: …the taste of death. Adam can further in another manner be named heaven and earth, because he himself had a soul of heavenly nature, and his body drew its origin from the earth. For thus Scripture says

headnotes.la: Est praeterea et alia rationabilis intelligentia, qua primus parens noster debeat vocari coelum et terra. De eo namque Eva facta est; sicut scriptum est
headnotes.en: And there is besides another reasonable understanding whereby our first parent ought to be called heaven and earth. For of him Eve was made; as it is written

headnotes.la: …magis quam Deo peccando consenserunt, statim inanes et vacui a gratia Spiritus sancti et reliquis virtutibus, quibus antea refulgebant, remanserunt. Pari quoque sententia accipiendum est quod sequitur
headnotes.en: …ather than to God, remained at once void and empty of the grace of the Holy Spirit and of the remaining virtues wherewith they before shone. With a like sentence also is that to be taken which follows

headnotes.la: …fundior, tanto remota ambiguitate est tenebrosior. Nonne satis tibi videntur esse tenebrosi, qui putabant se posse latere a facie Dei? Sic nempe post transgressionem ipse ait pro se et pro sua conjuge
headnotes.en: …uity removed, is it dark. Do they not seem to thee to be dark enough, who thought they could lie hid from the face of God? For thus after the transgression he himself said for himself and for his wife

headnotes.la: Tenebrae ergo erant super faciem abyssi, quia obscuritas peccati, et defensionis audacia, et involucrum mendacii obsidebat corda eorum, qui illum fallere verbis nitebantur, cui Salomon ait
headnotes.en: …upon the face of the deep, because the obscurity of sin, and the boldness of self-defence, and the wrapping of lying beset the hearts of those who strove to deceive with words him to whom Solomon says

headnotes.la: …ari, ut intelligamus jam nunc ex eo tempore gratiam baptismi per virtutem Spiritus sancti consecrari, quo baptismo progenies Adae ab hac transgressione debebat purificari. Sed et illud quod Deus dixit
headnotes.en: …ady from that time the grace of baptism was consecrated by the power of the Holy Spirit, by which baptism the offspring of Adam was to be purified from this transgression. And that also which God said

headnotes.la: …nter ipsi Adae aptari valet. Ipse enim quasi lux prae caeteris creaturis, quibus praelatus erat, emicuit, ideoque participatione sapientissimae lucis, quae in eo latebat, omnibus rebus nomina imposuit
headnotes.en: …elf. For he shone forth as it were a light before the other creatures over which he was set, and therefore by participation of the most wise light which lay hid in him he imposed names upon all things

headnotes.la: …in eodem statu, in quo ab eo conditus fuerat. Sed quia ipse peccavit, magna divisio fuit inter illum statum, quem ante lapsum habuit, et illum in quo post libamen peccati remansit, et haec est divisio
headnotes.en: …nded by him. But because he himself sinned, there was a great division between that state which he had before the fall, and that in which he remained after the tasting of sin; and this is the division

headnotes.la: quod est dicere: Ante transgressionem Adam justus, id est lux et dies exstitit; post transgressionis reatum, nox et tenebrae, id est peccator permansit
headnotes.en: which is to say: Before the transgression Adam stood just, that is, light and day; after the guilt of transgression he remained night and darkness, that is, a sinner

headnotes.la: Si per mane animam Adae quae coelestis naturae erat, et per corpus ejus vesperam volumus intelligere, potest talis solutio haberi hujus sententiae
headnotes.en: If by the morning we would understand the soul of Adam, which was of heavenly nature, and by his body the evening, such a solution of this sentence may be had

headnotes.la: …est gaudium et laetitia, jubilatio et exsultatio, et jucunditas indeficiens sanctorum suorum. Quod autem ipse Dominus Jesus filius sit Abrahae secundum carnem, testatur Matthaeus evangelista cum dicit
headnotes.en: …dness, the jubilation and exultation, and the unfailing delight of his saints. But that the Lord Jesus himself is the son of Abraham according to the flesh, Matthew the evangelist attests when he says

headnotes.la: …onis mysterium. Deambulatio quippe sancti Isaac in agrum insinuat nobis adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi in hunc mundum. Unde et Sponsa sua charissima eidem Domino Jesu dicit in Canticis canticorum
headnotes.en: …ion. For the walking of holy Isaac into the field insinuates to us the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ into this world. Whence also his most dear Bride says to the same Lord Jesus in the Song of Songs

headnotes.la: …udit; quam Dominus noster Jesus Christus finito certamine hujus saeculi introducet ad coelestis gloriae mansiones aeternas, cujus equidem Ecclesiae fundatoribus, scilicet sanctis apostolis, ipse dicit
headnotes.en: …m our Lord Jesus Christ, the contest of this world being finished, shall bring in to the eternal mansions of heavenly glory — to the founders of which Church, namely the holy apostles, he himself says

headnotes.la: …tulas sic alloquitur, dicens: *Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua* [n: (Cant. I)]. Sane quis est iste rex a quo ista Sponsa se dicit introductam esse in cellaria? Ille nimirum de quo propheta David ait
headnotes.en: …ng: *The king hath brought me into his storerooms* [n: (Cant. I)]. Truly, who is this king by whom this Bride says she has been brought into the storerooms? He assuredly of whom the prophet David says

headnotes.la: Quod utique idem rex summi regis filius in Evangelio manifestat clarius cum dicit
headnotes.en: Which indeed the same king, son of the highest king, makes plainer in the Gospel when he says

headnotes.en: But what are these storerooms, if not those tabernacles or courts of which David the prophet sang
