headnotes.la: …sa per patriarchas et reges, et per beatam Mariam originem duxit. Qualiter autem Judaei qui sunt matris ejus, scilicet Synagogae filii, contra ipsum in passione pugnaverunt, Psalmista testatur, dicens
headnotes.en: …archs and the kings, and through blessed Mary. But in what manner the Jews, who are the sons of his mother, that is, of the Synagogue, fought against him in the passion, the Psalmist testifies, saying

headnotes.la: … Christum, in tantum ut etiam vana sollicitudine illius custodirent sepulcrum, et quanto magis illum a se per incrudelitatem ejecerunt, tanto magis illum ad gentes, quae erant crediturae transmiserunt
headnotes.en: …licitude they even kept watch over his sepulchre; and the more they cast him out from themselves through their [sic: *incrudelitatem*], the more they sent him over to the Gentiles, who were to believe

headnotes.la: …eis gentium, quando nolentes credere in eum, a cordibus suis expulerunt illum. Et tunc Christus vineam suam non custodivit, quando eos exigente perfidia sua dereliquit. Unde et ipse in Evangelio dicit
headnotes.en: …lieve in him, they drove him out from their hearts. And then Christ did not keep his own vineyard, when he forsook them, their own faithlessness requiring it. Whence he himself also says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS QUOMODO ISTA SENTENTIA, SCILICET,
headnotes.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING HOW THIS SENTENCE, NAMELY,

headnotes.la: …ucta: Nigra sum propter inobedientiam et peccatum primi Adae patris mei, sed formosa futura sum propter obedientiam et justificationem secundi Adae, scilicet Christi redemptoris mei. Unde Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: …f the disobedience and the sin of the first Adam my father, but I shall be comely on account of the obedience and the justification of the second Adam, that is, of Christ my redeemer. Whence Paul says

headnotes.la: … vicinis suis, sic ego amodo instabilis ero et nunquam in eodem statu permanebo propter superbam spem inanis gloriae quam mihi diabolus falso spopondit, quando ad credendum sibi mihi persuasit, dicens
headnotes.en: … this time on I shall be unstable and shall never remain in the same state, on account of the proud hope of empty glory which the devil falsely promised me, when he persuaded me to believe him, saying

headnotes.la: …solem tentationem accipimus, verum et probatissimum sensum habemus. Dicit enim Dominus in Evangelio de seminibus supra petram seminatis, id est de infidelibus Christianis et perversis haereticis, quia
headnotes.en: …take temptation, we have a true and most approved sense. For the Lord says in the Gospel concerning the seeds sown upon the rock, that is, concerning unbelieving Christians and perverse heretics, that

headnotes.la: hoc est orta tentatione in fide et operatione defecerunt. Denique in libro Psalmorum scriptum reperitur
headnotes.en: …g. Luc. 8:6 *natum aruit*, "having sprung up it withered"; *sole orto* belongs to Matth. 13:6, where the verb is *aestuaverunt*, "they were scorched"] Finally in the book of Psalms it is found written

headnotes.la: …oloravit. *Filii matris meae pugnaverunt contra me.* Mater nostrae et angelicae naturae clementissima gratia est Creatoris Dei, a qua mirabiliter sunt creati homines et angeli, sicut dicitur in Genesi
headnotes.en: …mother have fought against me.* The mother of our nature and of the angelic nature is the most clement grace of God the Creator, by which men and angels were wonderfully created, as is said in Genesis

headnotes.la: …er serpentis suggestionem crudeliter expulerunt. *Posuerunt me custodem in vineis; vineam meam non custodivi.* Possumus istam sententiam secundum illum sermonem interpretari de quo scribitur in Genesi
headnotes.en: … through the suggestion of the serpent. *They have set me keeper in the vineyards; my vineyard I have not kept.* We can interpret this sentence according to that word of which it is written in Genesis

headnotes.la: …ut videlicet cogitando et loquendo quod Deo placitum esset, operaretur, et seipsam custodiret, ne a diabolo deciperetur. Quasi vero vineis paradisi nostra natura praelata fuit, quando a Domino audivit
headnotes.en: …ing what should be pleasing to God, it might work and might keep itself, lest it be deceived by the devil. And our nature was as it were set over the vineyards of paradise, when it heard from the Lord

headnotes.la: …tra tentationibus diversis et innumerabilibus fatigata, spinis et aculeis, calamitatibus et miseriis suae carnis vallata, putredine et corruptione suae carnis vel corporis aggravata: *nigra sum,* quia
headnotes.en: … temptations, walled about with the thorns and the stings, the calamities and the miseries of its flesh, weighed down with the rottenness and the corruption of its flesh or body: *I am black,* because

headnotes.la: …odo subjunxit qualiter nigra sit, scilicet, *sicut tabernacula Cedar.* Hoc est pigra et instabilis sum in bonum, prona vero et labilis sum ad malum. De isto autem Cedar conqueritur Psalmista cum dicit
headnotes.en: …manner she is black, namely, *as the tents of Cedar.* That is, I am sluggish and unstable toward the good, but prone and slippery toward the evil. But of this Cedar the Psalmist complains when he says

headnotes.la: id est cum his qui tenebras diligunt, et instabiles mente et corpore existunt. Unde Dominus ad Ezechielem loquitur dicens
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Psal. CXIX, 5 *habitationibus Cedar*, "the dwellings of Cedar"] that is, with those who love darkness, and are unstable in mind and in body. Whence the Lord speaks to Ezechiel, saying

headnotes.la: …ersum mundum vagaris, et immundis et tetris turpibusque intus cogitationibus devastaris, scito te habitare cum habitantibus Cedar. Sed et hoc quod sequitur in eodem versu, valde timendum est, scilicet
headnotes.en: …t laid waste within by unclean and foul and shameful thoughts, know thou that thou dwellest with the inhabitants of Cedar. But this also which follows in the same verse is greatly to be feared, namely

headnotes.la: …a mea cum habitantibus Cedar, hoc est cum vitiis et concupiscentiis, cum voluptatibus et immundis desideriis, quae omnia Cedar, id est tenebrae sunt, quia hominem tenebrosum faciunt. Unde Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: …y long with the inhabitants of Cedar, that is, with vices and concupiscences, with pleasures and unclean desires, all which are Cedar, that is, darkness, because they make a man dark. Whence Paul says

headnotes.la: id est peccatores;
headnotes.en: that is, sinners;

headnotes.la: … sum sicut pellis Salomonis.* Per quam pellem Salomonis diximus superius totum tabernaculum designari, quod de pellibus constructum fuit. Sed necesse est ut aliquid de eo secundum moralitatem loquamur
headnotes.en: …the skin of Solomon.* By which skin of Solomon we said above that the whole tabernacle is designated, which was built of skins. But it is necessary that we say somewhat of it according to the morality

headnotes.la: …uotidiano conflictu adversus animam praelientur, experimento satis probabili possumus indicare. Nonne visus pugnat adversus animam quando oculus videt mulierem ad concupiscendam eam? Unde Jeremias ait
headnotes.en: …ey war in daily conflict against the soul, we can show by an experience convincing enough. Does not sight fight against the soul when the eye sees a woman so as to lust after her? Whence Jeremias says

headnotes.la: … exterioribus delectationibus inficit, quasi vulneribus inflictis illam debilitat et occidit. Os vero nostrum quomodo mentiendo animam interficiat, Salomon interrogatus respondeat, sic enim ipse dicit
headnotes.en: …And while it infects him with outward delights, it weakens and kills her as with wounds inflicted. But how our mouth by lying slays the soul, let Solomon, being asked, answer, for thus he himself says

headnotes.la: Quod profecto David testatur, dicens in libro Psalmorum
headnotes.en: Which David assuredly testifies, saying in the book of Psalms

headnotes.la: Et Dominus in Evangelio
headnotes.en: And the Lord in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …placita sunt, tunc os nostrum nos justificat. Quibus vero telis tactus oppugnet animam, noverunt milites Christi, qui quotidie praeliantur spiritualia praelia Domini. Unde et divina Scriptura testatur
headnotes.en: …g to God, then our mouth justifies us. But with what darts touch assaults the soul, the soldiers of Christ know, who daily fight the spiritual battles of the Lord. Whence Holy Scripture also testifies

headnotes.la: QUALITER ISTA SENTENTIA,
headnotes.en: HOW THIS SENTENCE,

headnotes.la: …a Judaeorum crucifixum, sanguine suo perfusum; nigra, inquam, prae tristitia praesenti sum, quia dolor anxietatis filii mei pertingit usque ad dolorem cordis mei. Unde et Simeon ad beatam Mariam dixit
headnotes.en: …e Jews, drenched with his own blood; black, I say, am I by reason of present sadness, because the pain of my son's anguish reaches even to the pain of my heart. Whence Simeon also said to blessed Mary

headnotes.la: …quoniam ipsa Synagoga, id est perfidi Judaei illam quasi sororem suam spreverunt, et eam honorare noluerunt, justo Dei judicio, in hoc saeculo et in die judicii, ejus intercessione et auxilio carebunt
headnotes.en: …ss Jews, spurned her as though she were their sister, and would not honor her, by the just judgment of God, both in this world and in the day of judgment, they shall lack her intercession and her help

headnotes.la: …quae Topazion appellatur, ubi idem lapis topazius invenitur. Quod autem de Aethiopia topazius veniat, Dominus, ad beatum Job loquens, manifestat. Cum enim ad eumdem Job Dominus loqueretur de sapientia
headnotes.en: …n, where that same stone, the topaz, is found. And that the topaz comes from Ethiopia, the Lord, speaking to blessed Job, makes plain. For when the Lord was speaking to that same Job concerning wisdom

headnotes.la: …retiosi, nisi duodecim apostoli supra fundamentum, quod est Christus, fundati? Quem vero alium significat topazius rarior et pretiosior caeteris lapidibus, nisi Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui est
headnotes.en: …ones, if not the twelve apostles founded upon the foundation which is Christ? And what other does the topaz signify, rarer and more precious than the other stones, if not our Lord Jesus Christ, who is

headnotes.la: et est humilior omnibus hominibus? Inde etiam discipulis suis ipse in Evangelio fertur dixisse
headnotes.en: and is humbler than all men? Hence also he himself is reported in the Gospel to have said to his disciples

headnotes.la: Unde bene dicitur quod topazius omni resplendeat colore, quia
headnotes.en: Whence it is well said that the topaz shines back with every color, because

headnotes.la: et ipse decoratus est ornatu omnis spiritualis virtutis, quia secundum Joannem,
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. *in ipso inhabitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter*, adding "bodily"] and he himself is adorned with the adornment of every spiritual virtue, because according to John,

headnotes.la: … delectantur nomine Christi insigniri. Sane quod nos sanctam Ecclesiam insulae comparavimus, secundum Isaiam prophetam locuti sumus, qui omnes Ecclesias per prophetiae spiritum appellat insulas dicens
headnotes.en: …h the name of Christ. Assuredly, in that we have compared holy Church to an island, we have spoken according to Isaiah the prophet, who by the spirit of prophecy calls all the Churches islands, saying

headnotes.la: …aquam ejus divinitati comparare possumus ipsius humanitatem, quia aequalis est Patri secundum divinitatem, minor vero Patre secundum humanitatem. Hoc denique idem Filius manifestat in Evangelio dicens
headnotes.en: …pare his humanity to his divinity, because he is equal to the Father according to divinity, but less than the Father according to humanity. This, lastly, the same Son makes plain in the Gospel, saying

headnotes.la: quod pertinet ad ejus divinitatem; et alio loco
headnotes.en: which pertains to his divinity; and in another place

headnotes.la: quod pertinet ad ejus humanitatem. Unde et David propheta testatur in Psalmis
headnotes.en: which pertains to his humanity. Whence also David the prophet bears witness in the Psalms

headnotes.la: …mne nomen, accepit, ut in nomine ejus omne genu flectatur, et ab omni creatura coeli et terrae [n: (Philip. II)], cum Patre et Spiritu sancto unus Deus adoretur. Et hoc est quod in isto versu sequitur
headnotes.en: …me every knee should bow, and that by every creature of heaven and of earth [n: (Philip. II)] he should be adored as one God with the Father and the Holy Spirit. And this is what follows in that verse

headnotes.la: …e reperire non possum, et hoc est quod sequitur: *Ne forte vagari incipiam per greges sodalium tuorum,* quaerendo te sic, ut quondam illi vagabantur et errabant, de quibus in Evangelio Dominus dicebat
headnotes.en: …ma above, *ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum*, "lest I begin to wander after the flocks"] seeking thee thus, as once those men wandered and erred of whom in the Gospel the Lord was saying

headnotes.la: … Audierant enim prophetas miracula fecisse sicut Christum, quod est coloris aurei esse sicut topazium. Sed Petrus Spiritu sancto revelante aliis lapidibus relictis, verum topazium agnovit quando dixit
headnotes.en: …d wrought miracles as Christ did, which is to be of a golden color as the topaz is. But Peter, the Holy Spirit revealing it, the other stones being left aside, acknowledged the true topaz when he said

headnotes.la: … in Patre et Pater in Filio ineffabiliter ab aeterno maneat, omnis auctoritas tam Novi quam Veteris Testamenti consona voce praedicat. Unde est illud quod Dominus loquitur ad Patrem de discipulis suis
headnotes.en: …the Son ineffably from eternity, every authority of the New as well as of the Old Testament proclaims with concordant voice. Whence is that which the Lord speaks to the Father concerning his disciples

headnotes.la: Et alio in loco dicit Dominus ad Philippum
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Joan. XVII, 21, *ut omnes unum sint, sicut tu, Pater, in me, et ego in te, ut et ipsi in nobis unum sint*, without *volo*] And in another place the Lord says to Philip

headnotes.la: …et pascat Christus: nunc restat ut a nobis ostendatur, ubi in divinis eloquiis Deus Pater meridies appelletur, quia hoc raro imo rarissime reperitur, et quanto rarius tanto pretiosius. Deus omnipotens
headnotes.en: …s that it be shown by us where in the divine oracles God the Father is called midday, because this is rarely, nay most rarely, found, and the more rarely, by so much the more preciously. God almighty,

headnotes.la: cui displicent mala quae facimus, et cui placent bona quae agimus, ipse loquitur in Isaia propheta, dicens
headnotes.en: to whom the evils displease which we do, and to whom the goods please which we perform, himself speaks in Isaiah the prophet, saying

headnotes.la: …llius sit qui rem aut nescit, aut non intelligit? Ipse enim scit et intelligit omnia antequam fiant. Quae est ergo requies Dei, nisi pax in corde fidelis Christiani et religiosi? Sic enim scriptum est
headnotes.en: …ds it not? For he himself knows and understands all things before they come to be. What then is the rest of God, if not peace in the heart of a faithful and religious Christian? For thus it is written

headnotes.la: Et in Isaia invenimus dicentem Dominum
headnotes.en: And in Isaiah we find the Lord saying

headnotes.la: Magnam igitur requiem Deo nostro damus, quando peccatorem lapsum ut a peccato suo convertatur, exhortamur. Et alibi dicit Scriptura
headnotes.en: …y" — plural imperative, and *lassum* "weary" for *lapsum* "fallen"] Great rest therefore do we give to our God, when we exhort the fallen sinner to be turned from his sin. And elsewhere Scripture says

headnotes.la: [n: (Isa. LXVI.)] Quis autem est locus Dei, nisi pax et justitia, pietas et misericordia, et omnium virtutum mater obedientia? Inde dicit David propheta
headnotes.en: …gard, but to the poor little one and contrite of spirit"] And what is the place of God, if not peace and justice, piety and mercy, and obedience the mother of all virtues? Hence David the prophet says

headnotes.la: …. In qua si quis usque ad ultimum diem vitae suae meruerit perseverare, sine dubio usque ad contemplandum divinae majestatis claritatem poterit pervenire. Sic enim dicit divina Scriptura de obedientia
headnotes.en: …to persevere unto the last day of his life, without doubt he will be able to come even to the contemplating of the brightness of the divine majesty. For thus Holy Scripture speaks concerning obedience

headnotes.la: … quod ipse secundum Job prophetam [n: (cap. XXXI)] omnes gressus, id est opera nostra dinumerat, ut videlicet post mortem unicuique nostrum secundum quod egerit reddat. Sic enim dicit Paulus apostolus
headnotes.en: … Job the prophet [n: (cap. XXXI)], numbers all our steps, that is, our works, so that, namely, after death he may render to each one of us according to what he has done. For thus says Paul the apostle

headnotes.la: …erna morte pereamus, sed postquam hic vixerimus, alibi judicabimur, ut aut pro bonis operibus praemia consequamur aeterna, aut pro peccatis nostris supplicia perpetua consequamur. Unde et Propheta ait
headnotes.en: …but after we have lived here, we shall be judged elsewhere, that either for good works we may obtain eternal rewards, or for our sins we may obtain perpetual punishments." Whence also the Prophet says

headnotes.la: id est ab aeterno immobiliter statuit et praedestinavit. Quid?
headnotes.en: that is, from eternity he unchangeably established and predestined it. What?

headnotes.la: Quae sunt? Omnis
headnotes.en: What are they? All

headnotes.la: …ericordia. Ecce habes alterum. Quia tu reddes in die judicii unicuique secundum opera sua [n: (Apoc. XXII)]. Quod autem ad Filium, et non ad Patrem pertineat judicium, audi ipsum in Evangelio dicentem
headnotes.en: …he other. For thou wilt render in the day of judgment to every man according to his works [n: (Apoc. XXII)]. And that judgment pertains to the Son, and not to the Father, hear him saying in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Considerat ergo Deus Pater omnipotens in loco suo quasi meridiana lux omnia quae in hoc saeculo facimus, ut per Filium suum nobis reddat in die judicii secundum quod meruimus. Unde scriptum est
headnotes.en: …rs in his place, as the midday light, all the things which we do in this world, that through his Son he may render to us in the day of judgment according to what we have deserved. Whence it is written

headnotes.la: …adiis admirabilis suae claritatis totum mundum illuminat, sic Deum omnipotentem considerata ejus omnipotentia et misericordia omnis creatura contremiscit et adorat. De qua misericordia dicit Psalmista
headnotes.en: …rightness poured out everywhere, illumines the whole world, so every creature, his omnipotence and mercy being considered, trembles before God almighty and adores him. Of which mercy the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: et iterum
headnotes.en: and again

headnotes.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS, QUALITER AD PERSONAM PATRIS REFERRI DEBEAT ISTA SENTENTIA, SCILICET,
headnotes.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING, IN WHAT MANNER THIS SENTENCE OUGHT TO BE REFERRED TO THE PERSON OF THE FATHER, NAMELY,

headnotes.la: …supernae rorationes, quaeve sit terra inferius jacens vel satietas et ebrietas fructuum Dei subtiliter requiramus. Aeternos montes illos arbitror debere intelligi, de quibus Psalmista ad Dominum dicit
headnotes.en: …ove are, or what is the earth lying beneath, or the satiety and drunkenness of the fruits of God. Those, I judge, ought to be understood as the eternal mountains of which the Psalmist says to the Lord

headnotes.la: …m, per eloquia prophetarum, per doctrinam apostolorum Christianae religionis fidem agnovimus, qui prius remoti longe a cognitione Dei in tenebris et in umbra mortis sedebamus, unde Isaias propheta ait
headnotes.en: …apostles we came to know the faith of the Christian religion — we who before, removed far from the knowledge of God, were sitting in darkness and in the shadow of death; whence Isaiah the prophet says

headnotes.la: …icata, et sicut coeperunt in se Christum habere habitatorem, qui prius in cordis hospitio recipiebant diabolum pessimum seductorem, et animarum suarum crudelissimum interfectorem. Unde et Paulus dicit
headnotes.en: … to have Christ as an indweller within them, who before were receiving into the lodging of the heart the devil, that most wicked seducer and most cruel slayer of their own souls. Whence also Paul says

headnotes.la: Denique et beatus Augustinus
headnotes.en: [var: Vulg. Ephes. III, 17, *in cordibus vestris*, "in your hearts"] And lastly blessed Augustine

headnotes.la: Luce ergo clarius constat quia, nisi lumen fidei in cordibus nostris resplendeat, in tenebris infidelitatis sedebimus, et Christum habitatorem nullatenus habebimus. De his montibus Psalmista dicit
headnotes.en: …er than light that, unless the light of faith shine back in our hearts, we shall sit in the darkness of unbelief, and shall in no wise have Christ as an indweller. Of these mountains the Psalmist says

headnotes.la: Quod petra Christum significet Paulus apostolus edocet, dicens
headnotes.en: That the rock signifies Christ, Paul the apostle teaches, saying

headnotes.la: …rum se non dubitat, divina aspiratione tactus ad Christum, qui est vera petra, redire festinat, qui sinum clementiae, et fontem pietatis et misericordiae mortalibus aperiens, per prophetam suum clamat
headnotes.en: …touched by a divine inbreathing it hastens to return to Christ, who is the true rock — who, opening to mortals the bosom of clemency and the fountain of tenderness and mercy, cries through his prophet

headnotes.la: … et orationes salvantur, sic miseri, desperati et peccatorum suorum spinis circumdati, a Christo recipiuntur, si tamen ad extremam vitae suae horam ad ipsum convertantur. Sic enim divina Scriptura ait
headnotes.en: …he wretched, the despairing, and those hedged about with the thorns of their own sins are received by Christ, if only at the last hour of their life they be turned to him. For thus Holy Scripture says

headnotes.la: Ecce ostendimus Deo adjuvante quantum potuimus, quid sint aeterni montes; nunc restat ut demonstremus quid sint supernae rigationes. Moyses namque dicit
headnotes.en: …us fuerit ab impietate sua*] Behold, God helping, we have shown as much as we could what the eternal mountains are; now it remains that we demonstrate what the waterings from above are. For Moses says

headnotes.la: …tes; nunc restat ut demonstremus quid sint supernae rigationes. Moyses namque dicit: « Concrescat ut pluvia doctrina mea, et fluat ut ros eloquium meum [n: (Deut. XXXII)]. Isaias quoque ait ad Dominum
headnotes.en: … remains that we demonstrate what the waterings from above are. For Moses says: « Let my doctrine gather as the rain, and let my speech flow as the dew [n: (Deut. XXXII)]. Isaiah also says to the Lord

headnotes.la: …nifestum est ergo quod divinae Scripturae appellentur rigationes supernae, quibus rigati sunt prophetae et apostoli, et velut ore coelesti fecundati. De ista rigatione Paulus apostolus loquitur dicens
headnotes.en: …Holy Scriptures are called the waterings from above, by which the prophets and apostles were watered, and as it were made fruitful by a heavenly mouth. Of this watering Paul the apostle speaks, saying

headnotes.la: De hac iterum roratione coelesti David loquitur dicens
headnotes.en: …Heb. VI, 7, *Terra enim saepe venientem super se bibens imbrem, et generans herbam opportunam illis a quibus colitur, accipit benedictionem a Deo*] Of this heavenly bedewing again David speaks, saying

headnotes.la: Civitas vero Dei est corpus vel anima viri justi, quae plenius tunc laetificatur, quando fluentis divinorum eloquiorum delectabiliter irroratur. Hinc iterum David dicit
headnotes.en: And the city of God is the body or the soul of a just man, which is then more fully made joyful, when it is delightfully bedewed by the streams of the divine utterances. Hence again David says

headnotes.la: …li, et sciant procul dubio quia quanto amplius huic mundo et suae carni male vivendo serviunt, tanto longius a Deo recedunt, et diabolo crudeli dominatori se conjungunt. Sic enim ait Joannes apostolus
headnotes.en: …e more they serve this world and their own flesh by living wickedly, by so much the further do they withdraw from God, and join themselves to the devil, that cruel lord. For thus says John the apostle

headnotes.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS, QUALITER AD PERSONAM PATRIS REFERRI DEBEAT ISTA SENTENTIA, SCILICET,
headnotes.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING, IN WHAT MANNER THIS SENTENCE OUGHT TO BE REFERRED TO THE PERSON OF THE FATHER, NAMELY,

headnotes.la: …lucidare conabitur quae sit illa felix et beata terra quae de fructu operum Dei satiatur. Sane de terra locuturi, non longe a nobis recedamus, quia nos ipsi terra sumus. Sic enim dicit Dominus ad Adam
headnotes.en: …th is which is satisfied from the fruit of God's works. Assuredly, being about to speak of earth, let us not withdraw far from ourselves, because we ourselves are earth. For thus the Lord says to Adam

headnotes.la: …e non possit. Sed jam nunc ad terram redeamus de qua paulo ante loqui coeperamus. Terra quae data est diabolo in cibum, Judaei erant qui Dominum Jesum interficere cupiebant. Quibus et ipse Dominus ait
headnotes.en: …return to the earth of which we had begun to speak a little before. The earth which was given to the devil for food was the Jews, who desired to kill the Lord Jesus. To whom the Lord himself also says

headnotes.la: … patrem vestrum sequentes me vultis interficere, et in me qui sum veritas, nec vultis stare, nec credere. Nos ergo simus illa terra quae fructificans a Domino benedictionem percepit, sicut David dicit
headnotes.en: … your father, will to kill me, and in me, who am the truth, you will neither to stand nor to believe. Let us then be that earth which, bearing fruit, has received blessing from the Lord, as David says

headnotes.la: …asi spiritali potu debriatae gaudia hujus mundi pro nihilo ducunt, quia ad ipsum cujus cognitio est vita aeterna, spreta saeculi fallaci gloria pervenire contendunt. Unde idem Dominus in Evangelio ait
headnotes.en: …, count the joys of this world as nothing, because, the deceitful glory of the world being despised, they strive to come to him whose knowledge is eternal life. Whence the same Lord says in the Gospel

headnotes.la: …am, nostra tunc fructum suum dabit, quando corpus nostrum, per bona opera quae modo agit post hujus vitae fragilis terminum multis tentationibus probatum Deo reddet spiritum suum, dicens cum Psalmista
headnotes.en: …l then yield her fruit when our body, proved by many temptations through the good works which it now performs, shall after the end of this frail life render its spirit to God, saying with the Psalmist

headnotes.la: … sustinuerunt pro Deo poenas et tribulationes, sic post diem judicii pari gaudio recipiant illius summae et incomparabilis gloriae promissas a Deo mansiones. De quibus idem Dominus discipulis suis ait
headnotes.en: …and tribulations for God, so after the day of judgment they may with equal joy receive the mansions of that highest and incomparable glory promised by God. Of which the same Lord says to his disciples

headnotes.la: … Opera autem Dei generaliter sive universaliter omnes creaturae sunt, quae ab ipso Deo sapientissima ordinatione creatae sunt. De qua admirabili creatione sic protestatur auctoritas divinae Scripturae
headnotes.en: …nd the works of God, generally or universally, are all creatures, which were created by God himself with a most wise ordering. Of which wondrous creation the authority of Holy Scripture thus testifies

headnotes.la: Unde David propheta ad Dominum dicit
headnotes.en: Whence David the prophet says to the Lord

headnotes.la: …eus omnia in sapientia sua fecit, quia in Filio suo, qui est ejus sapientia et verbum et virtus, cuncta ineffabiliter condidit. Quod idem propheta in Spiritu sancto sentiens alio loco declarat, dicens
headnotes.en: …hings in his wisdom, because in his Son, who is his wisdom and word and power, he ineffably founded all things. Which the same prophet, perceiving in the Holy Spirit, declares in another place, saying

headnotes.la: …horum elementorum omnes creaturas quae a Deo creatae sunt, esse credimus. Quod Moysen eximium prophetarum in Spiritu sancto sensisse arbitrantur, qui de creatione mundi edisserens sic loquitur, dicens
headnotes.en: …od are within the compass of these elements. Which they judge that Moses, the choicest of the prophets, perceived in the Holy Spirit, who, discoursing of the creation of the world, thus speaks, saying

headnotes.la: …tera opera quae Deus omnipotens per Filium suum condidisse creditur, quoddam admirabile et speciale opus idem Filius fecisse legitur. De quo opere Isaias propheta divino spiritu tactus ita protestatur
headnotes.en: …ighty is believed to have founded through his Son, the same Son is read to have done a certain wondrous and special work. Of which work Isaiah the prophet, touched by the divine spirit, thus testifies

headnotes.la: RECAPITULATIO A SUPERIORIBUS, QUALITER AD PERSONAM PATRIS REFERRI DEBEAT ISTA SENTENTIA, SCILICET,
headnotes.en: RECAPITULATION FROM THE FOREGOING, IN WHAT MANNER THIS SENTENCE OUGHT TO BE REFERRED TO THE PERSON OF THE FATHER, NAMELY,

headnotes.la: …ascendit, et sic demum de arcanis et mysticis rebus cum Domino soliloquium habuit: sic sancta Ecclesia fecerat. Quasi enim montem magnum excelsumque ascendit, quando ad soliloquium Sponsi sui, qui est
headnotes.en: …a soliloquy with the Lord concerning secret and mystical things, so holy Church had done. For she ascends as it were a great and lofty mountain when she came to the soliloquy of her Bridegroom, who is
